To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding of 4-nitrosaminoquinoline 1-oxide or 2-acetoxymidopyrido[1, 2-a:3, 2'-d] imidazole to the c-Ha-rass proto-oncogene in vitro induces the mutation in the twelfth coden of the ras gene in NIH 3T 3 mouse fibroblasts and the transformation of the cells.

the ultimate carcinogens N-OAc-Glup-1 and N-OAc- 4AQO can transform mammalian cells, and that this transformation is caused by mutations in the region of CCGG in the eleventh and twelfth codons of the human c-HARAS-1 gene.
the ultimate carcinogen, N-OAc-Gliu-P-l, generates transforming activity in NIH 3T 3 cells and that this activity is associated with mutations in the twelfth codan of the Ha-ras gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the direct demonstration that chemical modification of the proto-oncogene c-Ha-rasl with ultimate carcinogens causes cellular transformation, and that this is the result of the formation of a specific mutation.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of the mutagenic and transforming activities of carcinogens, especially those that cause mutations in the ras proto-oncogene.
the chemical modification of plasmid DNA containing the human c-ras-1 gene, and the subsequent transformation of mammalian NIH 3T 3 cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of N-OAc-Glup-1 or N- OAc-4AQOs to the c-Ha-r as-1 gene is responsible for the induction of transformation in mammalian cells.
the chemical modification of plasmid DNA with N-OAc- G lu-P-1 or its analogues, N-OAc- 4AQO, causes cellular transformation.
DNA damage by ultimate carcinogens can cause cellular transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chemical modification of DNA by ultimate carcinogens can cause the activation of cellular proto-oncogenes and that this activation can result in the induction of transformation.
chemical transformation is induced by the binding of carcinogens with DNA and that the transformed cells are derived directly from the DNA adducted cells.
DNA adduct formation with ultimate carcinogens is a sufficient cause for transformation of cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA adducts formed with these chemicals are mutagenic in mammalian cells, and that the mutations are responsible for the transformation.
chemical carcinogens are capable of directly inducing the mutation of cellular oncogenes, and that such mutations may play a critical role in the process of chemical carcinogenesis.
chemical modification of DNA can induce the formation of an active oncogene.
